newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close below 2,100 support level.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close below 2,100 support level.

text.p: Singapore shares closed down on Friday in thin volume, with interest focused on small situational stocks, brokers said.
As investors stayed sidelined, the key Straits Times Industrials Index fell 13.64 points, easing below the 2,100 support level to close at 2,096.70.
"This spells trouble. I see the index slipping still lower to the 2,000 level next week," said an institutional dealer.
"If the index slips below 2,000 it would mean those who predicted a recovery only in 1997 were probably right," he said.
Brokers said the market believed a hike in interest rate.
"But it has already taken into account such a raise in interest rate by the United States," one broker said.

Malaysia's property firm Sri Hartamas topped volume with 8.67 million shares. It was up Singapore $0.04 (US$0.03) at S$1.01 after reporting an 18-month net profit of 9.5 percent and news of MBf Holdings' interest to double its stake in the company.

Oil rig-repair company Far East Levingston Shipbuilding (FELS) rose sharply before the close, gaining S$0.35 to S$7.35 on volume of 623,000 shares. Brokers said FELS rose on rumours the company was close to winning a US$250 million contract. -- US$1=S$1.41
